dedupe_keys.name: utd19 multi city urban traffic loop detector dataset

description: UTD19 is a large urban traffic data set from 23,541 stationary detectors on urban roads in 40 cities worldwide, described by its makers as the largest publicly available multi-city traffic data set. The Institute for Transport Planning and Systems at ETH Zurich collected it in a research campaign from 2017 to 2019. It consists mainly of loop detector measurements of vehicle flow and occupancy (or speed) at 3 to 5 minute intervals, about 170 million rows and 4.9 billion detected vehicles over 3.8 years of data, error-flagged and standardised, with detector locations and roads geocoded in WGS84 for map matching. Cities include Augsburg, Basel, Bern, Birmingham, Bordeaux, Hamburg, London, Los Angeles, Madrid, Melbourne, Paris, Taipei, Tokyo, Toronto, Utrecht, Vilnius and Zurich. Access: free after signing up and agreeing to the project's conditions. Caveats: periods and detector density differ by city, and use is bound by the sign-up conditions. The data underpin studies of empirical macroscopic fundamental diagrams and network capacity, and support calibration of urban network flow and capacity models. They complement the METR-LA and PEMS-BAY benchmarks and the Seattle loop detector data set catalogued here.
